title: Round 8 / ECDLP-25: Lean x-only interpolation bound for k (linear) on short Weierstrass curves
question: Using the CurveX/Interpolation infrastructure, determine and formally prove the best degree lower bound for g in F[X] with g(x(kP)) = k for 1 <= k <= N < r/2 (x-only interpolation of the discrete log itself), or record why the second-difference argument degenerates.
claims: Lean-verified (mathlib pinned, no extra axioms): if g in F[X] satisfies g(x(kP)) = k for 1<=k<=N, 2N<r, P of order r on short Weierstrass with 2!=0, then N <= 3 deg g + 2; for odd r and N=(r-1)/2, r <= 6 deg g + 5. Declarations in MathResearch/ECDLP/LinearInterp.lean. The cleared second-difference polynomial N0 has degree exactly 3 deg g (leading coeff -2 lc g), so it never degenerates; 3 != 0 not needed. Bound not shown tight (numerics: interpolant has deg g = N-1). Polynomial degree only; says nothing about bit complexity or existence of g. Independent review pending.
next_action: PI: add 'import MathResearch.ECDLP.LinearInterp' to MathResearch.lean, run independent review (docs/REVIEW.md), then update ledger; optional: seek tighter bound using higher-order differences.
notes: Adapter frontmatter model claude-sonnet-5-5; runtime identity not exposed to PI. Formalization agent self-reported model identity: claude-sonnet-5-5 (Sonnet 5.5); not independently verifiable.
